summary: This work introduces U-TRACK, a family of dynamical decoupling sequences designed using optimal tracking that enforces identity evolution at intermediate checkpoints in addition to the end of the sequence, preventing error accumulation across pulse blocks. Experimental validation on superconducting-qubit platforms demonstrates that U-TRACK4 maintains superior robustness against static detuning and amplitude errors compared to XY4 and UR40, while simulations show it outperforms both sequences under low-frequency random telegraph noise.
motivation: Conventional DD sequences accumulate residual errors over repeated cycles, degrading performance during long idle times, while single-block optimization methods like UR40 are fragile to mid-sequence parameter changes. Combining the block-by-block refocusing of periodic sequences with global optimization would provide both robustness and resilience to time-dependent noise.
method: The authors generalized the optimal tracking framework from NMR to a universal (state-independent) setting, optimizing pulse phases of $M$ blocks with $N$ pulses each to maximize average fidelity at all intermediate waypoints using GRAPE with a genetic algorithm for global search. Sequences of 40 $\pi$-pulses (10 blocks of $N=4$) were optimized over $\delta/(2\pi) \in [-1.5625, 1.5625]$ MHz and $\epsilon \in [-0.4, 0.4]$ on a transmon qubit with $T_\pi = 128$ ns.
result: At $T = 5.12$ µs, U-TRACK4 maintains high process fidelity across all intermediate times whereas XY4 shows systematic error accumulation and UR40 exhibits fragmented robustness profiles; under random telegraph noise at $\lambda = 0.5$ MHz with $\delta/(2\pi) = \pm 0.5$ MHz, UR40 achieves $\bar{F} \approx 0.54$ while U-TRACK4 and XY4 achieve $\bar{F} \approx 0.92$, with U-TRACK4 maintaining better performance at high detuning amplitudes.
